全能的光盘盘面可见图像生成与刻录工具

Disc Image Studio 是一个多平台的光盘盘面图像生成与刻录工具，帮助您使用任何刻录光驱在任何 DVD / CD / 单层蓝光 光盘上刻蚀出肉眼可见的图像。 ![.NET 版本](https://img.shields.io/badge/.NET-10.0-512bd4?style=flat-square) ![运行平台](https://img.shields.io/badge/Platform-Windows%20%7C%20Linux%20%7C%20macOS-0078d6?style=flat-square) ![开发语言](https://img.shields.io/badge/Language-C%23-68217A?style=flat-square) ![GitHub Repo size](https://img.shields.io/github/repo-size/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio?style=flat-square&color=3cb371) ![贡献欢迎](https://img.shields.io/badge/PRs-Welcome-brightgreen?style=flat-square) [![许可证：GPL-3.0-or-later](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-GPL--3.0--or--later-blue?style=flat-square)](LICENSE)
--- ## 效果预览 ![](docs/images/case1.jpg) ![](docs/images/case2.jpg) --- ## 概述 Disc Image Studio 可将一张图片转换成符合 CD、DVD 与单层 BD-R 光盘物理层约束的数据，刻录后将使光盘盘面呈现肉眼可见的图案。 ## 界面预览 ![主页：模板与最近工程](docs/images/ui-home.png) ![设计页：图层画布与影调](docs/images/ui-design.png) ![导出页：浅色主题与输出镜像](docs/images/ui-export.png) --- ## 快速开始 Windows 下载 `win-x64.exe` 后可直接运行。Linux 或 macOS 请下载与 CPU 匹配的**实验性 CLI** 压缩包，解压后运行 `./disc-image-studio --help`。这些发布包均自带 .NET 运行时。 [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/releases) ### 1. 新建工程 在主页选择 CD、DVD 或蓝光，指定输出位置后创建工程。 ### 2. 设计盘面 在设计页导入图片，用图层完成排版，并在右栏「影调」模块调整抖动、伽马、亮度与灰阶档位。 ### 3. 预览与导出 在预览页核对盘面投影，在导出页生成 ISO / RAW / WAV+CUE，或使用即时刻录功能直接写入空白盘片。 即时刻录为实验性功能，请只使用可报废的测试介质。 ## 功能 ### 光盘数据生成 - **CD 支持**：支持任何 CD 。您可导出带格式头的 WAV 音轨及配套 CUE，兼容 cdrecord, ImgBurn等刻录软件；也允许导出 RAW 音轨。详见 [CD 刻录兼容说明](docs/CD_AUDIO_COMPATIBILITY.md)。 - **DVD 支持**：支持任何 DVD。您可导出 ISO 镜像。 - **蓝光支持**：支持任何单层 BD-R 25 GB，支持纯绘图与 UDF 2.01 文件。详见 [ADDING_BLURAY.md](docs/ADDING_BLURAY.md)。 - **随盘文件**：CD／DVD／蓝光可在设计页直接选择要保存的文件夹及内圈／外圈位置，也可在导出页调整；设置随工程保存。 - **文件区域预览**：混合盘的设计投影和成品读回用黄色标出文件区（含文件系统）。 - **介质灰度方案**：CD 与 DVD 均使用黑白二阶，CD 使用 `0D / AA`，DVD 扰码域使用 `A5 / 92`。详见 [PHYSICAL_MODEL_AUDIT.md](docs/PHYSICAL_MODEL_AUDIT.md)。 - **灰度抖动工具**：独立程序也可将原图处理为 `0/255` 黑白二阶 PNG；支持打开或拖入原图、并排预览及无损 PNG 导出。详见[使用与构建说明](tools/FourLevelDither/README.md)。 - **盘片预设**：内置数个品牌的光盘参数，覆盖 CD／DVD／BD。您也可将自己标定好的数据贡献给我们，详见[预设维护说明](docs/DISC_PRESETS.md)。 ### 辅助标定 Disc Image Studio 提供粗标定、边界标定和精细标定流程，通过盘面照片估计内外半径与轨距分布。下面的历史实盘对比中，校准前采用恒定轨距，十字线的径向线条出现明显弯曲；使用辅助标定得到的三次轨距参数重新生成并刻录后，线条更接近径向直线。实测精度取决于照片矫正、取点和复刻验证，参数保存的小数位数不代表测量精度。 | 校准前 · 恒定轨距 | 校准后 · 三次轨距 | | --- | --- | | ![校准前的 DVD 实拍：径向十字线明显弯曲](docs/images/verbatim-dvd-calibration-before.jpg) | ![校准后的 DVD 实拍：径向十字线更接近直线](docs/images/verbatim-dvd-calibration-after.jpg) | | `P20261004-133519.jpg` | `P20261004-135416.jpg` | 第一次使用可跟随[DVD 标定实操教程：Verbatim AZO DVD-R](docs/CALIBRATION_TUTORIAL.md)，查看照片矫正、三个标定阶段的实际取点、参数变化与参考值，以及精标后的盘面效果。完整流程与参数说明见[辅助标定说明](docs/CALIBRATION.md)。 ### 刻录 - **镜像文件输出**：您可以导出完整 ISO / RAW 文件并使用合适的刻录软件手动刻录。 - **即时流式刻录（实验性）**：CD、DVD 与 BD-R 边生成边刻录，不保存完整镜像；BD-R 走 MMC 顺序写入。 - **不要使用非空白介质！** ## 系统与设备要求 - 桌面版需要 Windows 10 2004（2004/20H1，19041）及以上，或 Windows 11。 - 构建：.NET 10 SDK（`global.json` 锁定 10.0.x）；自行构建的非自包含 GUI 需要 .NET 10 Windows 桌面运行时。Release EXE 已包含运行时，无需另行安装 .NET。 - “即时刻录”功能需要一台 Windows 可识别的 CD / DVD / BD 刻录机与空白盘片；BD-R 需要支持顺序写入的单层空白盘。 ## 构建与运行 ```powershell dotnet build DiscImageStudio.slnx --configuration Release dotnet run --project src/DiscImageStudio.App --configuration Release ``` 构建回归检查： ```powershell dotnet run --project src/DvdImageSolver --configuration Release -- selftest dotnet run --project tests/DiscImageStudio.ArchitectureTests --configuration Release ``` 版本规则、CI 生成 EXE、Release 草稿检查、MSIX 打包与签名流程见[发布指南](docs/RELEASING.md)。 ## 命令行 Linux（glibc）可选 `linux-x64` 或 `linux-arm64`。Apple Silicon Mac 选 `osx-arm64`，Intel Mac 选 `osx-x64`。CLI 在本地生成镜像，实际写盘可交给支持相应镜像或音轨的刻录软件。 使用 .NET 10 SDK 从源码运行 CLI ```sh dotnet run --project src/DiscImageStudio.Cli -c Release -- --help ``` CLI 可读取 PNG、JPEG、BMP 和 GIF，使用动画图片的第一帧。下面的例子用两扇区音轨验证安装，同时生成配套 CUE。 ```sh ./disc-image-studio cd-generate --input picture.png --output sample.wav --sectors 2 ``` | 命令 | 说明 | | --- | --- | | `solve` | 使用固定快速纹理映射（CW 方向）生成 DVD 镜像，黑白纹理可选抖动混合 | | `encode` | 将单个 DVD ECC 块编码为 NRZI 通道电平 | | `calibrate` | 标定投影：按生成几何从 DVD 源图片取样，按实测几何投到盘面 | | `simulate` | 按实测半径对生成的 DVD ISO 做读回模拟 | | `selftest` | 运行 DVD 引擎的确定性回归自检 | | `cd-generate` | 无随盘文件时生成 WAV + CUE / RAW 音轨；指定 `--data-dir` 时生成 CD 数据盘 ISO | | `cd-preview-warp` | 标定投影：按实测几何投影 CD 源图片 | | `cd-preview-track` | 按标定几何渲染已有的 WAV 或 RAW CD-DA 音轨（读回模拟） | | `bd-generate` | 生成完整 BD-R ISO，并写出 `.json` sidecar | | `bd-info` / `bd-probe` / `bd-encode` | 导出 BD 参数、原始负载探针或单个 ECC 簇诊断 | 各命令的完整参数见对应文档。 ## 源码结构 ```text src/DiscImageStudio.Cli/ Linux 和 macOS 离线命令行入口 src/DiscImageStudio.ImageIO/ WIC 和跨平台图像编解码 src/DiscImageStudio.Core/ 介质无关的模块契约、工程/预设模型、任务与命令目录 src/DiscImageStudio.Imaging/ CD/DVD/BD 共用的图片预处理与抖动辅助 src/DiscImageStudio.Burning/ Windows IMAPI2 设备枚举、流缓冲与安全刻录层 src/DiscImageStudio.Cd/ CD-DA 生成核心与 CD 模块 src/DiscImageStudio.Dvd/ DVD 引擎适配模块 src/DiscImageStudio.BluRay/ BD-R 几何、17PP/ECC、3T/6T 映射、流式生成与 ISO src/DiscImageStudio.Iso/ UDF 2.01 / ISO9660 写入器 src/DiscImageStudio.App/ WPF GUI、统一命令行与商店资源 src/DvdImageSolver/ 保持隔离的 DVD 编码/求解引擎 tests/ 无第三方测试框架的架构回归测试 packaging/ MSIX 清单与打包脚本 tools/ 独立辅助工具与资产生成脚本 docs/ 架构、引擎、预设、发布等文档 ``` ## 隐私与安全 - Disc Image Studio 不联网、不上传文件、不收集遥测，详见[隐私政策](PRIVACY.md)。 - 发现安全问题请不要在公开 Issue 中披露，按[安全政策](SECURITY.md)使用 GitHub 私密报告。 ## 贡献 欢迎报告问题与提交代码。开发环境搭建、模块边界规则、测试要求与 Pull Request 流程见[贡献指南](CONTRIBUTING.md)。 ## 许可证 项目采用 [GNU GPL v3.0 or later](LICENSE)（`GPL-3.0-or-later`）。CD 交织实现包含从 CDImage 移植并修改的代码，整体分发沿用兼容的 GPL 授权；分发二进制或修改版时须遵守对应源代码等要求。第三方字体与组件遵循各自许可证，详见 [授权说明](LICENSE-NOTICE.md) 和 [第三方声明](THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt)；应用"关于"页也可离线查看完整文本。 ## Unlock datacenter-class intelligence on the hardware you already own — Run 290B+ frontier MoE models locally on your gaming PC at blistering interactive speeds. ## About FreeToken is an edge-native Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) serving engine designed for running frontier-scale open-weight models on personal and consumer hardware. It treats heterogeneous edge resources—GPUs, CPUs, host memory, and interconnects—as a unified, elastic inference platform. Its core features include: - **Fast Edge-Native Runtime**: Provides efficient MoE serving with bandwidth-adaptive CPU–GPU co-execution ($q^\star$ policy), full-layer double-buffered prefill streaming, global LRU expert caching, graph-compatible execution, and the FTW fast weight format. - **Semantic-Aware Caching**: Features semantic anchor checkpoints for recurrent state and KV caches, allowing agentic context edits (e.g., tool calls, thinking blocks) to avoid redundant context recomputation. - **Elastic Memory Management**: Supports dynamic, runtime VRAM re-allocation between expert caches and KV memory without engine restarts or weight reloading. - **Broad MoE & Ecosystem Support**: Supports frontier open-weight MoE models (e.g., DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, GLM-5.2) across various parameter scales and quantization formats (e.g., MXFP4, NVFP4, FP8, BF16, GGUF), with Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible APIs for seamless integration with real-world coding and tool-calling agents (e.g., Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, OpenClaw, DeepSeek Harness). - **Diverse Consumer Hardware**: Scales across consumer laptops, gaming desktops, and workstation GPUs, with native support for NVIDIA RTX 30, RTX 40, and RTX 50 series GPUs. ## Getting Started ### Desktop app Download FreeToken for Windows or Linux at [flashml.ai](https://www.flashml.ai/). It sets the engine up for you and gives you a GUI for running models, chatting, and tuning the engine.
### CLI Install FreeToken with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (recommended) or pip: ```bash uv pip install "freetoken[accel]" ``` Or build from source: ```bash git clone https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken.git && cd FreeToken uv venv && source .venv/bin/activate uv pip install -e ".[accel]" ``` For More details: - [Install FreeToken](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/blob/main/docs/install.md) - [Quick start](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/blob/main/docs/quickstart.md) - [Supported models](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/blob/main/docs/models.md) - [CLI reference](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/blob/main/docs/cli.md) - [Repairing old FTW checkpoints](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/blob/main/docs/ftw-hotfix.md) - [Diagnosing a checkpoint that fails to load](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/blob/main/scripts/checkpoint_diagnose/README.md) ## Citation If you use FreeToken for your research, please cite our [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16157): ```bibtex @article{yang2026freetoken, title={FreeToken: Efficient Edge-Native MoE Serving with Bandwidth-Adaptive Execution}, author={Yang, Shuo and Fan, Xiaoze and Pan, Melissa and Xi, Haocheng and Wang, Zhe and Sun, Shanlin and Keutzer, Kurt and Han, Song and Zaharia, Matei and Xu, Chenfeng and Stoica, Ion}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2608.16157}, year={2026} } ``` ## Acknowledgment FreeToken was deeply inspired by [mini-sglang](https://github.com/sgl-project/mini-sglang), and learned the design and reused code from the following projects: [SGLang](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang), [vLLM](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm), [FlashInfer](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer), [flash-linear-attention](https://github.com/fla-org/flash-linear-attention), [LightLLM](https://github.com/ModelTC/lightllm) and [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp). ## License [Apache License 2.0](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/blob/main/LICENSE).

Monty the Clapper — the official mascot of OpenMontage

OpenMontage

The first open-source, agentic video production system.

Paste A Video  ·  Quick Start  ·  Try These Prompts  ·  Pipelines  ·  How It Works  ·  Providers  ·  Review Guide  ·  Agent Guide

Follow The Build

--- > **Something new is taking shape.** > > We're building something new for creatives, and we're looking for curious minds to try it early. > > **[Curious? Take a first look and join the early users.](https://github.com/calesthio/OpenMontage/discussions/892)** Turn your AI coding assistant into a full video production studio. Describe what you want in plain language — your agent handles research, scripting, asset generation, editing, and final composition. **Important distinction:** OpenMontage can make image-based videos, but it can also make a real **video video** for free/open-source workflows: the agent builds a corpus from free stock footage and open archives, retrieves actual motion clips, edits them into a timeline, and renders a finished piece. That is not the usual "animate a handful of stills and call it video" trick.
> **"SIGNAL FROM TOMORROW"** — a cinematic sci-fi trailer fully produced through OpenMontage: concept, script, scene plan, Veo-generated motion clips, soundtrack, and Remotion composition.
> **"THE LAST BANANA"** — a 60-second Pixar-style animated short about a lonely banana who finds friendship with a kiwi. 6 Kling v3-generated motion clips (via fal.ai), Google Chirp3-HD narration, royalty-free piano music, TikTok-style word-level captions, and Remotion composition. Total cost: **$1.33**.
> **"OBJECTS IN OVERDRIVE"** — a 54-second, music-driven 3D showcase featuring ten objects with distinct choreography: gravity-shifting furniture, frozen car drifts, cloth impacts, refractive lenses, moving gears, an acrobatic robot, and more. Custom Blender animation and physics, kinetic typography, and a phonk soundtrack. Rendered with Blender Eevee/Cycles and assembled with FFmpeg. No narration.
> **"Reimagine Your Universe"** — a 50-second vertical transformation film in which one visual idea moves across objects, eras, materials, and scale. Five generated motion scenes, sparse Google Chirp narration, a Pixabay score, and a bespoke HyperFrames composition turn separate clips into one authored cinematic journey. Total cost: **about $4**.
> **"Products Come to Life"** — a 60-second product film built from approved hero stills. Five hard-surface products separate into their own engineering and reassemble, with each still pinned as the first and last frame so the model invents motion without losing product identity. Image-to-video generation, bespoke sound, narration, and a custom composition complete the film.
> **"Imagine the Possibilities with OpenMontage"** — seven generated worlds collected into one music-only showcase. Three image models supply campaign, fashion, and miniature-world artwork; four video models expand the journey through architecture, material transformation, a living greenhouse, and a creature encounter. OpenMontage animates the stills, edits the motion, unifies the soundtrack, and closes with Monty the Clapper. Source generation cost: **about $5**.
> **"How Salt Made History"** — a 100-second cinematic documentary about the mineral that funded empires, shaped trade routes, sparked revolutions, and gave us the word “salary.” Real-world footage is woven together with original narration and hand-authored motion graphics for its etched title, etymology reveal, animated maps, historical timeline, and closing thesis.
> **"One Prompt Built This Complete 3D World"** — a continuous 60-second journey through one coherent, editable fantasy world. Distinct terrain regions, an inhabited village, waterways, ruins, dense vegetation, and a late hero-landmark reveal are assembled from textured 3D assets, then brought together with cinematic lighting, atmospheric music, and a planned camera path.

Subscribe to @OpenMontage on YouTube to see new videos as they ship — every video includes the full prompt, pipeline, tools used, and cost so you can reproduce it yourself.

--- ## Start From A Video You Already Love Starting from a reference video is often faster than starting from a blank prompt. OpenMontage can start from a **YouTube video, Short, Reel, TikTok, or local clip** and turn it into a grounded production plan: 1. **Paste a reference video** 2. **The agent analyzes transcript, pacing, scenes, keyframes, and style** 3. **You get 2-3 differentiated concepts, an honest tool path, cost estimates, and a sample before full production** ```text "Here's a YouTube Short I love. Make me something like this, but about quantum computing." ``` What you get back is not "best guess prompt spaghetti." You get: - **What it keeps** from the reference: pacing, hook style, structure, tone - **What it changes**: topic, visual treatment, angle, narration approach - **What it will cost** at your target duration, before asset generation starts - **What it will actually look like** with your currently available tools Works with **Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, Codex** — any AI coding assistant that can read files and run code. --- ## Watch It Happen — The Backlot Living Storyboard Chat tells you what the agent *said*. **Backlot shows you what the production is actually doing** — a local board that fills itself in as the pipeline runs. Stages light up, the script lands as a screenplay page, scene cards shimmer while assets generate, and every provider decision and dollar spent is on the wall. When a production starts, the agent opens it for you automatically. No setup, no reporting — the board derives everything from the project files the pipeline already writes.

**The storyboard is now a real approval gate.** Asset generation pauses on a scene-by-scene contact sheet — takes, prompts, per-asset cost, quality scores — so you approve the visuals *before* the render, not after it's too late:

Creative gates hold until you answer. The board shows what's waiting and why; you reply in chat:

Every production on your machine, live-first, in the library:

```bash python -m backlot open # the library — every project on disk python -m backlot open # one production's live board python scripts/backlot_simulate_run.py # no production yet? watch a simulated one live ``` And when a run is done, hit **▶ REPLAY RUN** — the whole production replays from its timestamps, scrubbable end to end. See [`backlot/README.md`](backlot/README.md) for how it works. --- ## Quick Start ### Prerequisites - **Python 3.10+** — [python.org](https://www.python.org/downloads/) - **FFmpeg** — `brew install ffmpeg` / `sudo apt install ffmpeg` / [ffmpeg.org](https://ffmpeg.org/download.html) - **Node.js 18+** — [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/) - **An AI coding assistant** — Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, or Codex ### Install & Run ```bash git clone https://github.com/calesthio/OpenMontage.git cd OpenMontage make setup ``` Open the project in your AI coding assistant and tell it what you want: ``` "Make a 60-second animated explainer about how neural networks learn" ``` Or if you want the real-footage path: ```text "Make a 75-second documentary montage about city life in the rain. Use real footage only, no narration, elegiac tone, with music." ``` That's it. The agent researches your topic with live web search, generates AI images, writes and narrates the script with voice direction, finds royalty-free background music automatically, burns in word-level subtitles, and renders the final video. Before you see anything, the system runs a multi-point self-review — ffprobe validation, frame sampling, audio level analysis, delivery promise verification, and subtitle checks. Every provider selection is scored across 7 dimensions with an auditable decision log. Every creative decision gets your approval. > **No `make`?** macOS/Linux: `python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && python -m pip install -r requirements.txt && cd remotion-composer && npm install && cd .. && python -m

--- English | [简体中文](README_zh-CN.md)

Docs • Try it Now • Tutorials • Examples • Blog • Community [![PyPI version](https://badge.fury.io/py/kornia.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/kornia) [![Downloads](https://static.pepy.tech/badge/kornia)](https://pepy.tech/project/kornia) [![star](https://gitcode.com/kornia/kornia/star/badge.svg)](https://gitcode.com/kornia/kornia) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-5865F2?logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/HfnywwpBnD) [![Twitter](https://img.shields.io/twitter/follow/kornia_foss?style=social)](https://twitter.com/kornia_foss) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

**Kornia** is a differentiable computer vision library that provides a rich set of differentiable image processing and geometric vision algorithms. Built on top of [PyTorch](https://pytorch.org), Kornia integrates seamlessly into existing AI workflows, allowing you to leverage powerful [batch transformations](https://kornia.readthedocs.io/en/latest/get-started/gpu-acceleration.html), [auto-differentiation](https://kornia.readthedocs.io/en/latest/get-started/differentiability.html) and [GPU acceleration](https://kornia.readthedocs.io/en/latest/get-started/gpu-acceleration.html). Whether you're working on image transformations, augmentations, or AI-driven image processing, Kornia equips you with the tools you need to bring your ideas to life. > **📢 Direction**: Kornia is becoming the **reference implementation and executable specification** for differentiable computer vision and geometry in the PyTorch ecosystem — explicit conventions, conformance tests, and honest benchmarks over API growth. Read the [Roadmap](ROADMAP.md). ## When to use Kornia Kornia pays off where a hand-written version gets long or fragile, or where the alternatives leave the GPU: - **Breadth.** 1,200+ public operators, most with no torchvision equivalent: camera models and epipolar geometry, minimal solvers and RANSAC, feature detection, description and matching, edge detection, morphology, Lab and Bayer color, image losses and metrics. torchvision overlaps mainly on resizing, cropping, flipping, color jitter and blur. - **Per-sample parameters in one batched call.** `gaussian_blur2d(x, (9, 9), sigma)` takes a `(B, 2)` `sigma`; `rotate` takes a `(B,)` angle, `warp_affine` / `warp_perspective` take `(B, 2, 3)` / `(B, 3, 3)` matrices and `adjust_brightness` a `(B,)` factor. torchvision's functional ops apply one parameter per call. From Kornia 0.9.1, a `sigma` tensor and the enhancement value checks (gamma, contrast, solarize) are validated on the device, so a CUDA call, or an MPS call on PyTorch ≥ 2.13, needs no host synchronization for them. - **Batched minimal solvers and robust estimation.** `find_fundamental(x1, x2, method="7POINT")` solves `(B, 7, 2)` samples and returns all real solutions in `(B, 3, 3, 3)`, with zero matrices in the unused slots; the 8-point, 5-point essential (`find_essential`), DLT homography and PnP (`solve_pnp_dlt`) solvers are there too. `RANSAC` (homography, fundamental and essential models) samples and scores hypotheses on the device; by default its refinement and final selection run on the host in float64, and `compile=True` (PyTorch ≥ 2.14, CPU and CUDA) runs the whole estimation as one compiled graph on the device. - **Differentiable geometry.** Depth to 3D and back (`depth_to_3d_v2`, `unproject_points`, `project_points`), `warp_frame_depth`, `remap`, camera models with Brown–Conrady and Kannala–Brandt distortion, and Lie groups (`So3`, `Se3`) keep gradients with respect to depth, pose and camera parameters. - **Annotated augmentation.** `AugmentationSequential` applies one sampled transform to images, masks, boxes and keypoints together and can invert it, in 2D; the 3D augmentations transform volumes, without annotations or an inverse. On CUDA, augmentations move their sampled parameters to the GPU without blocking it, and a sync-guard test keeps every public augmentation free of avoidable host synchronizations. - **Local features on the GPU.** SIFT and HardNet, DISK, ALIKED, XFeat, DeDoDe, LoFTR and LightGlue, with mutual-nearest-neighbour and ratio-test matchers. - **Morphology** with arbitrary structuring elements on batched tensors. - **Compiles and exports.** Nearly all probed operator configurations run under `torch.compile` and match eager, and over 1,000 export to ONNX; the result for every operator is on the [export support page](https://kornia.readthedocs.io/en/latest/get-started/export-support.html). - **Fast where it is designed to be: batched tensors on a GPU.** In the published 0.9.0 flagship benchmarks (RTX 4090, batch 32), many filters, warps, feature-matching steps and image metrics run about 10× to 70× faster in eager mode than per-image OpenCV or scikit-image on the CPU, and `torch.compile` takes several of them past 100×. On the small overlap with torchvision on the same GPU, eager Kornia is slower; compiled Kornia is faster for hue, color jitter and Gaussian blur and still slower for flips, crops and brightness. OpenCV wins single-image `uint8` CPU work. Results vary with hardware and workload; every number, win and loss is published on the [performance page](https://kornia.readthedocs.io/en/latest/get-started/performance.html). These operators run on the input's device with no NumPy round trip, and most are differentiable; robust estimation (`RANSAC`) and the extraction methods of learned features such as DeDoDe and XFeat run without gradients. For a single fixed-parameter operation, such as one blur or one resize, a few lines of PyTorch or torchvision are just as good. ## Key Components 1. **Differentiable Image Processing**
Kornia provides a comprehensive suite of image processing operators, all differentiable and ready to integrate into deep learning pipelines. - **Filters**: Gaussian, Sobel, Median, Box Blur, etc. - **Transformations**: Affine, Homography, Perspective, etc. - **Enhancements**: Histogram Equalization, CLAHE, Gamma Correction, etc. - **Edge Detection**: Canny, Laplacian, Sobel, etc. - ... check our [docs](https://kornia.readthedocs.io) for more. 2. **Advanced Augmentations**
Perform powerful data augmentation with Kornia’s built-in functions, ideal for training AI models with complex augmentation pipelines. - **Augmentation Pipeline**: AugmentationSequential, PatchSequential, VideoSequential, etc. - **Automatic Augmentation**: AutoAugment, RandAugment, TrivialAugment. 3. **AI Models**
Leverage pre-trained AI models optimized for a variety of vision tasks, all within the Kornia ecosystem. - **Face Detection**: YuNet - **Feature Matching**: LoFTR, LightGlue - **Feature Descriptor**: DISK, DeDoDe, SOLD2 - **Segmentation**: SAM - **Classification**: MobileViT, VisionTransformer.

repos.description: Open-source, self-hosted alternative to Grok Bot, Claude Duet, OpenAI Dots, Meta Muse, Instinct, Manus Cue: AI coworkers (named agents) with instructions, memory, routines, their own isolated computer, and your approval before they act.
repos.readme:
# Open Duet **Build a team of AI coworkers and choose where they run.** Open Duet is an open-source workspace for creating named AI agents, giving them jobs and workspaces, and bringing them together to complete tasks. Keep useful context between conversations, run routines, and review actions before they make changes. Use the desktop app, run your own server, or visit the separate hosted service. Open Duet does not include an AI model or model subscription. You choose the engine and provider account used for your work. ## Project links - [GitHub repository](https://github.com/Anil-matcha/open-duet) - [Desktop downloads](https://github.com/Anil-matcha/open-duet/releases) - [Hosted app](https://suparagent.ai) - [Watch the demo](https://youtu.be/vtFy94DfETE) - [Quick start](#quick-start) - [Guides](#guides) - [Discord support](https://discord.com/invite/zpnuBRXhKg)

> **Status:** Open Duet is in active development. Desktop releases, self-hosting, > agent computers, and newer team features are still evolving. Review > [known limitations](#known-limitations) before relying on them for important work. ## Contents - [What you can do](#what-you-can-do) - [Ways to run Open Duet](#ways-to-run-open-duet) - [Hosted plans](#hosted-plans) - [Engines, data, and costs](#engines-data-and-costs) - [Known limitations](#known-limitations) - [Support](#support) - [Contributing](#contributing) - [License](#license) ## What you can do - **Create agents and teams.** Give agents a name, role, engine, workspace, memory, and approval settings. A lead can delegate work to specialists or coordinate agents in shared rooms. Team leads can use Claude or Codex. See [teams and delegated work](docs/TEAMS.md). - **Keep useful context.** Agents can save notes, recall relevant notes and conversations, and search their history. You can review and edit what they remember. See [memory](docs/MEMORY.md). - **Run work on a schedule.** Create routines for scheduled, webhook, or manual runs. Review each result and answer requests for approval; a routine never approves an action by itself. See [routines](docs/ROUTINES.md). - **Choose how much freedom agents have.** Use Ask first, Accept edits, Approve for me (Claude, Codex, and Cursor), or Plan only. Review tool activity and approval decisions in the app. - **Connect tools and apps.** Connect services such as GitHub, Gmail, and Google Calendar through your own Composio key, then grant access to selected Claude or Codex agents. Changes wait for your approval. Add individual tools from the MCP Marketplace. See [connected apps](docs/CONNECTED_APPS.md). - **See what needs your attention.** The Today view gathers approvals, questions, routine outcomes, engine failures, and due tasks. It can show read-only Gmail and calendar items. See [everyday features](docs/EVERYDAY.md). - **Plan and follow work.** Use a task board and calendar to assign work, schedule one-time runs, and review conversations and attempts. See [tasks and calendar](docs/TASKS.md). - **Reuse instructions.** Save skills and start agents from templates. Skills are instructions you choose for a message. See [skills](docs/SKILLS.md) and [templates](docs/TEMPLATES.md). - **Use it from your phone.** Pair the phone app with your own server to chat, stop an answer, allow or deny a tool call, or create and edit agents and rooms. See the [phone app guide](docs/MOBILE.md). - **Work with files and history.** Search conversations, attach text and images, import audio for transcription with your consent and credentials, browse or download workspace files, and export your history. ## Ways to run Open Duet | | Desktop app | Self-hosted server | Hosted web app | Development checkout | |---|---|---|---|---| | Best for | A personal workspace on your computer | Keeping your agents and routines available on a server you control | Using the separately operated Suparagent service | Contributing or changing Open Duet | | Where workspace data lives | Your computer | Your server | An account-specific hosted workspace | Your development machine or configured database | | Start here | [Quick start](#quick-start) | [Self-hosting guide](docs/SELF-HOSTING.md) | [suparagent.ai](https://suparagent.ai) | [Development setup](docs/SETUP.md) | | Main requirements | Node.js 22+, uv, and an engine | Linux server, HTTPS, Docker or Node.js and uv, and an engine | An account and an AI provider account | Node.js, uv, and Docker if you use PostgreSQL | | Status | Experimental | Experimental; single owner | Separate hosted product | — | The hosted service is separate from the open-source desktop and self-hosted core. Hosted account, workspace, and billing data are handled by Suparagent; see the hosted service's [Privacy Policy](https://suparagent.ai/privacy) and [Terms](https://suparagent.ai/terms). ## Hosted plans The hosted preview lets you use your own Boat key for sandbox compute. Paid plans use compute operated by Suparagent, so you do not need to supply a Boat key. In both cases, you bring your AI provider account and pay that provider for model usage. | Plan | Monthly Suparagent price | Included running compute | Machine disk capacity | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Free preview | $0 | Billed to your Boat account | Small profile | | Starter | $15 | 100 hours per billing period | 51 GB | | Standard | $49 | 300 hours per billing period | 51 GB | | Pro | $99 | 720 hours per billing period | 111 GB | Paid-plan compute hours count while the sandbox is running, including idle time. At the limit, it stops until the next billing period or a plan change; compute overages are not charged. The disk value is the selected machine's capacity, not a separate storage quota. A stopped sandbox's disk is subject to the provider's retention period, so export important files before a paid plan ends. Paid checkout is enabled for hosted accounts; see the [Suparagent pricing page](https://suparagent.ai/pricing/) for current plans. ## Engines, data, and costs Connect an engine you already use: Claude Code or Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Google Gemini through Antigravity, Cursor, another command-line agent using the Agent Client Protocol (ACP), OpenRouter, or an OpenAI-compatible API such as Ollama or LM Studio. Available tools vary by engine; image input and agent computers, for example, are not supported by every engine. See [engine setup and capabilities](docs/ENGINES.md). For desktop and self-hosted use, conversations, agent notes, routines, and settings are stored in that instance's local data folder or server database. Workspace files stay in the folders you assign to agents. API keys saved through Open Duet are encrypted there; command-line sign-ins remain with the engine installed on that machine. When an agent answers, the selected engine receives the prompt and the context needed for that turn. This can include text you attach, relevant notes, and workspace content the engine reads. If the engine is a hosted service, that information is handled under that provider's terms. You bring the provider account, CLI sign-in, or API key; model usage may cost money. ## Quick start The desktop app runs from a source checkout. It needs Node.js 22 or newer, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), and at least one engine available on the same computer. For a CLI engine, install it and sign in before opening Open Duet. You can also configure an API-based engine in **Settings → Engines**. Docker is only needed for the optional isolated agent computers. ```bash git clone https://github.com/Anil-matcha/open-duet.git cd open-duet/desktop npm run app ``` On first launch, choose an engine, workspace, and approval mode. Then: 1. Open **Settings → Engines** and confirm an engine is ready. 2. Create an agent with a name, a clear job, and a workspace. 3. Start a chat. Choose **Ask first** to pause for approval before actions that need it. 4. Add teammates or create a routine when you want to split up or repeat work. See the [Releases page](https://github.com/Anil-matcha/open-duet/releases) for current desktop installers and the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) for changes. Installers are experimental and unsigned. The assisted update flow offers a SHA-256-verified installer for you to open; it does not install updates automatically. The release-to-release update path has not been verified end to end. ## Example: prepare a weekly project briefing Create a lead agent and specialists, such as a researcher and an editor. Give them the same project workspace, and set the lead's engine to Claude or Codex. Ask the lead to prepare a briefing from the notes and reports in that folder. The lead can split the request into smaller tasks and hand them to the specialists. Their work runs in separate conversations, then returns to the lead to assemble. Follow along in chat and approve actions when the settings require it. Once the process works well, make it a weekly routine and review each run in the app. ## Scheduling tasks Routines run prompts on local agents on a schedule, by webhook, or on demand. They run in the backend, so the backend must stay running. The original Telegram bot and [Boat](https://docs.boat.dev/api-keys) sandbox task flow are optional and separate from the agent workspace. See [backend scheduling details](backend/README.md#scheduling) and [environment settings](backend/.env.example). ## Known limitations - Open Duet is early and changing. The self-hosted server is experimental and intended for one owner with paired devices, not a multi-user organization. - Team delegation is new; lead agents need to use Claude or Codex. - The phone app has been tried on an Android emulator and an Android phone, not on iOS. It has no push notifications or store release. - Docker computers, browser tools, and the macOS native desktop preview are experimental and opt-in. - Desktop installers are unsigned and have limited platform verification. See [desktop setup details](docs/SETUP.md#desktop-app-from-a-source-checkout-experimental). - Connected apps are reached through Composio and tested against a fake Composio service, not yet the real service. Only Claude and Codex agents can use them, and changes wait for your approval. - The MCP Marketplace, hosted cloud computers, quiet routine results, and audio transcription have not had live-service or packaged-app qualification. ## Guides **Getting started** - [First-run setup and approvals](docs/SETUP.md) - [Engines and models](docs/ENGINES.md) - [Self-hosting](docs/SELF-HOSTING.md) **Agents and work** - [Teams and delegated work](docs/TEAMS.md) - [Agent settings and chat management](docs/CHAT_MANAGEMENT.md) - [Memory and context](docs/MEMORY.md) - [Routines](docs/ROUTINES.md) - [Tasks and calendar](docs/TASKS.md) - [Everyday features](docs/EVERYDAY.md): search, attachments, audio, and Today **Tools and customization** - [Connected apps](docs/CONNECTED_APPS.md) - [App language settings](docs/LOCALIZATION.md) - [Skills](docs/SKILLS.md) and [templates](docs/TEMPLATES.md) - [Agent computers](docs/COMPUTERS.md), [native desktop](docs/NATIVE-DESKTOP.md), and [browser tools](docs/BROWSER.md) - [Features](docs/FEATURES.md) and [capability matrix](docs/CAPABILITIES.md) **Project** - [Roadmap](docs/ROADMAP.md) - [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) - [Phone app](docs/MOBILE.md) - [Contributing](docs/CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Support - Join the [Open Duet Discord community](https://discord.com/invite/zpnuBRXhKg) for questions and discussion. - Report bugs and request features in [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/Anil-matcha/open-duet/issues). - For hosted account or billing questions, use the contact link on [suparagent.ai](https://suparagent.ai/contact
